# NOTES: "The Movie Boys in Peril; or, Strenuous Days Along the Panama Canal" by Victor Appleton (Gutenberg #76378, Garden City Publishing, 1926). Single book, no separate BOOK headings.

## Front matter / series
- Series: The Famous Movie Boys. Prior titles mentioned: The Movie Boys on Call; in the Wild West; in the Jungle; in Earthquake Land; and the Flood (Mississippi). Next: "The Movie Boys Under the Sea; or The Treasure of the Lost Ship."
- Other series ads at back: Frank Allen series (Graham B. Forbes), Nat Ridley detective, Dave Fearless (Roy Rockwood).

## Characters
- **Joe Duncan** and **Blake Stewart**: "Moving Picture Boys," chums, operators. Blake = more serious, deeper thinker; Joe = impulsive, good with figures, has pending patent on a focusing tube for camera.
- **Mr. Calvert Hadley**: head of Film Theatrical Company, wrote letters. **Mr. Ringold**: dramatic end of company.
- **C. C. Piper ("Gloomy")**: grouchy actor; predicts boys "buried alive" under slide.
- **Birdie Lee** (pretty, vivacious; Blake's interest), **Mabel Pierce** (new member; Joe's interest), **Nettie Shay** (Miss Shay).
- **Hank Duryee**: town livery driver, Central Falls. Horse **Rex**.
- **Mr. Hiram Baker**: farmer-landlord near Central Falls; wife Mrs. Baker.
- **Vigues Alcando** (Mr. Alcando): Spaniard/South American, Equatorial Railroad Co. (later revealed as Brazilian railroad); accent, formal, dramatic; cut on head; calls himself "señor"-slip. Card engraved "Vigues Alcando."
- **Sam**: freckle-faced, red-haired barefoot boy, son of neighbor farmer; delivered delayed special delivery letter from father (postmaster Sim Rolinson).
- **Captain Watson**: commander of government tug *Nama*.
- **Captain Martail**: captain of Brazilian steamer that crashed into *Nama*; Alcando's distant relative.
- **Captain Wiltsey**: captain of tug *Bohio* (replacement); also Canal employee.
- **Ramo**: educated Indian guide in jungle, shot alligator.
- **General George W. Goethals**: chief engineer (mentioned).
- **Captain (unnamed) of Canal**; Indian messenger from tug.

## Chapter-by-chapter events
**Ch I – To the Rescue:** Blake & Joe at Baker farm near Central Falls, riding motor cycle (~90 mph capable). Joe hopes for Mabel's letter; Blake teases re Birdie. Runaway horse (Rex) pulls buggy with Hank and Alcando; a rein breaks. Broken bridge half mile beyond farmhouse over rocky ravine (~100 ft deep), condemned; temporary bridge; temporary road makes sharp turn. Boys ride motor cycle to head off runaway.

**Ch II – On the Brink:** Background on boys' career (Movie Boys on Call; West; Pacific/jungle; Earthquake Land; flood; Film Theatrical Co.). Chase; boys cut across meadow where bridge-building materials stored; motor cycle's gasoline pipe breaks. Horse goes through barrier fence, over bridge edge; carriage catches on a king beam and hangs.

**Ch III – A Surprise:** Boys pull carriage back. Hank and Alcando wedged; seat broke. Rex dead in ravine. Alcando wakes, Spanish accent. Boys fetch water from spring (Blake, drinking cup). Alcando's card. A letter addressed to Blake & Joe from Film Theatrical Co. falls from his pocket.

**Ch IV – A Delayed Letter:** Alcando says he came to learn moving pictures; Hadley's letter introduces him ("when you go to Panama"). Boys surprised—no prior Panama plans. Alcando explains he is with Equatorial Railroad, wants to film jungle railroad; came to NY, Hadley recommended boys.

**Ch V – Another Surprise:** Red-haired Sam delivers special delivery letter (Pa carried it in pocket). Blake reads Hadley's full letter (quoted): Culebra Cut slide expected, "monstrous big slide," based on a man who claims small slides followed by bigger one; warns of Alcando; Alcando "a gentleman" but "foreigner's views." Pay, expenses. "Johnnie on the Spot."
Boys ride home; Alcando hotel in Central Falls. Hank driven; Mr. Baker lends horse. Alcando to stay at Central Falls hotel a week.

**Ch VI – Something Queer:** Joe notes Alcando seemed sorry they saved him. Blake reads *History of the Panama Canal* from library: Culebra Cut 9 miles long, 120 ft avg depth, sides 500 ft above bed; French and US slide problems; ditch 800 ft wide at first, later 1,800 ft at top. Boys decide to go; write Hadley. Alcando's table papers hastily hidden. Wind blows letter: "... go to Panama, get all the pictures you can, especially the big guns...." Blake suspicious.

**Ch VII – In New York:** Alcando explains "guns/ones" as English error from friend. Boys decide to take him; Blake still suspicious. Final week at farm; Alcando left early for NY. Studio at NY: C.C. Piper says "buried alive under one of the big Culebra slides."

**Ch VIII – Off for Panama:** Hadley plan: steamer to Colon, Washington Hotel headquarters; government permits; tug through canal; films for Panama Exposition in California; Gatun locks scenes; jungle scenes. Hadley dismisses spy idea ("South America would work to preserve the Canal"). Boys visit Alcando at NY hotel; smell cigar smoke; box on table hidden. Sail on steamer *Gatun*; Birdie and Mabel wave; Piper: "look out for the big slides."

**Ch IX – The Little Box:** Voyage to Colon (stop at San Juan, Porto Rico). Alcando buys excess gear. Ticking heard in Alcando's berth; brass-bound box with metal projections. Alcando says it's his new alarm clock (invention).

**Ch X – The Secret Conference:** Joe suspects bomb; Blake calm. Alcando angry, then explains invention. Arrive Colon; Washington Hotel. Balcony conference at night: "Are you sure the machine works right?" "Perfectly... every test."

**Ch XI – Along the Canal:** Joe's focusing tube patent. Tug *Nama* with Capt. Watson. Runner (Spanish) tells Alcando: "You will not fail us?" "I will not fail—if I have to sacrifice myself." Canal lock explanation: Gatun locks 85 ft up; Pedro Miguel 30⅓ ft; Miraflores 54⅔ ft. Breakwater 11,000 ft. Ditch 500 ft wide, 40 ft deep, 7 miles.

**Ch XII – Almost an Accident:** Lock details: steel chain fender (3-inch links, 100-ton yield, breaks ~250 tons); emergency dams (2 min electric, 30 min hand). Tug backward between gates due to signals failure; stopped in time.

**Ch XIII – In the Jungle:** Locks: 46 gates; 600 tons; 65 ft wide, 7 ft thick; water through 70 floor openings. Gatun Dam: 1½ mile long, 105 ft high. Captain says dynamite is only real danger. Alcando: "dynamite... would make a wonderful scene." Trip up Chagres River to Gamboa.

**Ch XIV – In Dire Peril:** Jungle: leaf-cutting ants, tapirs, orchids ("Holy Ghost"), iguanas (legs crossed, fattened), mamaei and sapodilla fruit. Blake swims; alligator; Ramo shoots it; Blake cramp from plantains.

**Ch XV – In Culebra Cut:** Week in jungle. Culebra Cut at Gold Hill. Alcando mutters "dynamite here, or at the dam, would do the work."

**Ch XVI – The Collision:** Alcando claims "abstract" remark. Boys stay two weeks at Culebra. Hadley letter praises work. Tug reaches central pier at Pedro Miguel/Miraflores approach; Brazilian steamer (Captain Martail) crashes into *Nama*.

**Ch XVII – The Emergency Dam:** *Nama* sinks (seams opened); boys save cameras; wreck raised later. Moved to *Bohio*. Blake senses something; Alcando visits about double exposure.

**Ch XVIII – The Big Slide:** Upper gate misopened at Miraflores flood; boys film flood; emergency dam swung into place. Alcando: "You are very brave." Rumors. Culebra Cut big slide alarm.

**Ch XIX – Joe's Plight:** Slide on Gold Hill. Joe buried; camera tripod. Alcando goes with Blake.

**Ch XX – At Gatun Dam:** Blake and Alcando dig; find Joe under rubber coat wrapped around face; cut on forehead. Joe okay, doctor at Gatun. Blake films dredging.

**Ch XXI – Mr. Alcando's Absence:** Blake a week at Culebra; General Goethals orders men. Joe suspicious; overheard Alcando: "I just hate to do it... I'll not put the blame on..." Blake: Alcando a failure as operator. Alcando goes off with small camera; ticking case heard.

**Ch XXII – A Warning:** Alcando says alarm clock. Blake reads Alcando's letter: "Stuff is all ready... get away... fine scenery in Europe." Blake discovers Alcando left camera & clock at dam. Captain Wiltsey: rumor dam to be dynamited tonight.

**Ch XXIII – The Flashlight:** Wiltsey explains plan; boys use flashlight powder (magnesium) and automatic trip-wire camera. Canal guards hidden. Boys wanted Alcando excluded (Spaniard).

**Ch XXIV – The Tick-Tick:** Boys place cameras near spillway; Joe fixes wire; ticking heard.

**Ch XXV – Mr. Alcando Disappears:** Blake cuts wires to brass box; flashlight; Alcando caught by guards near dam. Confesses: Brazilian railroad stockholder's plot to scare shippers, small charge, blame boys; box is timer. Alcando escapes overnight. Stockholder and Alcando later seen in European capital. Blake and Joe trip to Panama. Next volume: "The Movie Boys Under the Sea." Boys return to New York.

## Key quotes
- Hadley: "Johnnie on the Spot."
- Piper: "buried alive under one of the big Culebra slides."
- Alcando: "I will not fail—if I have to sacrifice myself."
- Alcando: "In my country, there is always mañana."
